prompt: Which expression gives the SI base units of the watt (W)?

answer.explanation: Power is work divided by time: 1 W = 1 J s^-1. Work is force times displacement: 1 J = 1 N m = (1 kg m s^-2)(1 m) = 1 kg m^2 s^-2. Dividing by seconds gives 1 kg m^2 s^-3.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 is correct. 1 W = 1 J s^-1 = 1 kg m^2 s^-3.
Option 2 is the SI base unit representation of the newton (N), the unit of force.
Option 3 is the SI base unit representation of the joule (J), the unit of work or energy.
Option 4 represents action or angular momentum (J s), not power.
hints: Express the watt in terms of joules and seconds: 1 W = 1 J s^-1.
Break down the joule into newton-metres, and newtons into base units using F = ma.
solution: 1 W = 1 J s^-1 = (1 N m) s^-1 = (1 kg m s^-2 * m) s^-1 = 1 kg m^2 s^-3. Option A is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Start with the definition P = W / t, so [P] = [W] / [t].
Use W = Fs and F = ma: [W] = kg * (m s^-2) * m = kg m^2 s^-2.
Divide by seconds: [P] = (kg m^2 s^-2) / s = kg m^2 s^-3.
